metadata.title: Carnell Tate Trending Up with Enormous Volume Share
metadata.description: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Carnell Tate has been one of the lone bright spots for his team this season. The No. 4 overall pick in this year's draft, Tate has quickly ascended into a high-volume role as one of quarterback Cam Ward's favorite targets. He has played at least 84% of the snaps in three of his first four NFL games, and he has seen his target total increase each of the last two weeks. He was especially dominant in Week 4, catching nine of 12 targets for 145 yards. The only blemish on his stat line was a lost fumble. Outside of the turnover, Tate proved that he is a consistent, reliable option for the Titans in the passing game, and the team should continue to feature him as they look to break out of a 0-4 start. Tate has surged into the mid-to-high WR2 tier for fantasy football, but managers must acknowledge that he has a slightly lower floor given that Ward is susceptible to dud outings as a passer.

metadata.title: Carnell Tate Has Biggest Day As A Pro In Loss
metadata.description: The Tennessee Titans lost yet another game, this time to the Baltimore Ravens by a score of 18-24. But rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate finally produced like a WR1, racking up 145 receiving yards with nine receptions on 12 targets. Tate has been getting open with regularity through his first three games, but the ineffectiveness of quarterback Cam Ward and the lackluster production of the offense have held him back. The Ravens have a strong secondary, but Tate proved why he was a first-round draft pick by getting open at all levels of the field. His target, reception, and yard totals were a season-high for him, and are good news for the future. He fumbled the ball twice, and lost one of those fumbles, so there are areas of his game he can clean up. But he's excellent at slamming on the brakes, which helped him get wide open on multiple catches. He also made strong grabs in tight coverage. A Week 5 matchup with the Houston Texans may make it tough for him to have another big game upcoming, but things are looking up for the rookie as a WR3/flex with upside.

metadata.title: Carnell Tate - Career-best day in loss to Ravens
metadata.description: Tate caught nine of 12 targets for 145 yards in Sunday's 24-18 loss to Baltimore.
metadata.analysis: While the fourth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft is still looking for his first career touchdown, Tate looked the part of a No. 1 wideout Sunday, as his 145 receiving yards were more than he'd produced in his first three games combined. He'll take a 22-268-0 line on 32 targets, and some real momentum, into a Week 5 home tile against the Texans, whose secondary just got shredded by CeeDee Lamb for 17 catches, 189 yards and a TD.

metadata.title: Carnell Tate eclipses 100 receiving yards in Week 4 loss
metadata.description: Carnell Tate caught 9-of-12 targets for 145 yards in the Titans loss to the Ravens Sunday .
metadata.analysis: Tate did fumble the ball twice, losing one after an impressive reception. He set new season highs in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in the loss. Tate and the Titans will look for their first win of the season as they take on Houston in Week 5.

metadata.title: Carnell Tate a Risky Start Amid Quarterback Concerns in Tennessee
metadata.description: The fourth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Tennessee Titans wide receiver Carnell Tate has gotten off to a slow start to his NFL career. Across three games, the 21-year-old has recorded 13 catches for 123 yards on 20 targets. On the bright side, Tate currently leads Tennessee in targets and is coming off his most productive performance in Week 3, hauling in six catches for 58 yards against the New York Giants. However, the Titans' passing game and offense as a whole remain a major question mark in quarterback Cam Ward's second season as the starter. Three games in, Ward is averaging just 5.7 yards per pass attempt, and the Titans as a team are averaging just 12.3 points per game. Without significant improvements in his offensive environment, Tate remains a risky start on a weekly basis for fantasy managers.

metadata.title: Carnell Tate leads team in receiving Sunday
metadata.description: Carnell Tate hauled in 6-of-9 targets for 58 yards in Sunday's 12-7 loss to the New York Giants.
metadata.analysis: The rookie was arguably the lone bright spot for the Titans on Sunday. He led the team with 58 receiving yards on the afternoon and flashed some real talent in the process. He's a good player but isn't likely to be a consistent fantasy producer on this offense, which is among the NFL's worst.

metadata.title: Carnell Tate - Volume steps up in Week 3 loss
metadata.description: Tate caught six of nine targets for 58 yards in Sunday's 12-7 loss to the Giants.
metadata.analysis: The fourth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft set new season highs in catches, targets and receiving yards while leading the Titans in the latter category, although Wan'Dale Robinson caught one more pass and was on the other end of Cam Ward's only TD of the day. Through three games, Tate leads the team with 20 targets, turning them into a modest 13-123-0 line in one of the league's weakest passing attacks. Tate will try to keep building chemistry with Ward in a Week 4 road trip to Baltimore.

metadata.title: Carnell Tate Difficult to Trust Amid Slow Start to 2026
metadata.description: The fourth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Tennessee Titans rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate has had a frustrating start to his NFL career. Across two games, the 21-year-old has recorded just seven catches for 65 yards on 11 targets. On the bright side, Tate leads Tennessee wide receivers in snaps and is the only player on the team who has reached double-digit targets. Unfortunately for fantasy managers, the Titans' passing game and offense as a whole remain rough in quarterback Cam Ward's second season at the helm. Through two weeks, Tennessee ranks 30th in the NFL in passing yards, and Ward has thrown just one touchdown pass. Better days could be ahead for Tate as both he and Ward continue to get reps at the NFL level. Still, in the short term, Tate is difficult for fantasy managers to trust.

metadata.title: Carnell Tate catches three passes in Week 2
metadata.description: Carnell Tate caught three of his five targets for 27 yards in a 24-20 loss to the Eagles in Week 2.
metadata.analysis: Tate finished fourth on the team in receiving yards in the close loss to Philly. The rookie has caught seven of his 11 targets for 65 scoreless yards through the first two games of the season. Tennessee will now get ready to take on the Giants in Week 3. Tate will be tough to start in fantasy until Tennessee's passing attack starts to show more life.

metadata.title: Carnell Tate - Nondescript day again in Week 2
metadata.description: Tate caught three of five targets for 27 yards in the Titans' 24-20 loss to the Eagles on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Tate's five targets paced the Titans, but eight different members of the team drew targets on a day Cam Ward attempted just 20 passes. It's become evident that Tennessee would prefer to hide Ward rather than highlight him, and therefore the offense is going to have a really tough time supporting any pass catchers as reliable fantasy starters. Tate has a measly seven catches for 65 scoreless yards on 11 targets through two career regular-season games. He won't be an exciting fantasy bet next Sunday against the Giants.

metadata.title: Carnell Tate is Underwhelming in NFL Debut
metadata.description: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Carnell Tate made his NFL debut against the New York Jets on Sunday. There was plenty of hype surrounding this debut after Tate was selected fourth overall during this year's draft. Tate didn't give fantasy managers a ton to be happy about on Sunday. The rookie wideout hauled in four of his six targets for 38 yards in the loss. The good news is that Tate finished tied for the team lead in receiving yards and targets with Wan'Dale Robinson. The entire Titans offense struggled to move the ball, and that could be a season-long theme. The hope is that things will get better for Tate once he builds more chemistry with quarterback Cam Ward. Fantasy managers should consider Tate a low-end WR3 for the Week 2 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.

metadata.title: Carnell Tate - Four catches in NFL debut
metadata.description: Tate caught four of six targets for 38 yards in Sunday's 23-10 loss to the Jets.
metadata.analysis: Tate tied Wan'Dale Robinson for the team lead in receiving yards and targets, but Tennessee's entire passing game struggled as Cam Ward threw for a mere 140 yards. The Titans overhauled their wide receiver room by drafting Tate fourth overall out of Ohio State and signing Robinson to a four-year, $78 million contract in the offseason, but the results Sunday didn't look much different compared to the team that went 3-14 last season. Tate should continue to function as one of Ward's top targets in Week 2 against a stout Eagles secondary.

metadata.title: Carnell Tate catches four passes in Week 1
metadata.description: Carnell Tate caught four of his six targets for 38 yards in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
metadata.analysis: Tate tied for the team lead in targets and receiving yards while finishing second in receptions in his NFL debut. The rookie receiver will surely have bigger games going forward, as the entire Tennessee offense struggled in the season opener. Tate will be a low-end WR3 heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Eagles.

metadata.title: Carnell Tate a Boom/Bust Flex Option for Fantasy Managers in Week 1
metadata.description: The fourth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Tennessee Titans wide receiver Carnell Tate enters his rookie season in a position with significant expectations. While Tennessee has a pair of capable veteran wideouts in Wan'Dale Robinson and Calvin Ridley, Tate profiles as the team's most explosive and highest-upside pass-catcher by far. In Week 1, Tate and the Titans get a favorable matchup against the New York Jets, who allowed the most receiving touchdowns (36) in the NFL last season. However, the offensive ecosystem around Tate remains a question mark. Titans quarterback Cam Ward largely struggled as a rookie in 2025 and put together a shaky preseason this summer. Tate carries significant upside if Tennessee can field a competent passing game, but the team may operate with a run-heavy approach in what projects to be a low-scoring game against the Jets. All in all, Tate profiles as a low-end WR3/flex option for fantasy managers on Sunday.

metadata.title: Carnell Tate - Off injury report
metadata.description: Tate (undisclosed) is off the injury report ahead of the Titans' season opener against the Jets, Turron Davenport of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: This is a great development for Tate after he dealt with an undisclosed issue late in preseason. Tate is now on track to make his NFL debut in Week 1, when he will be a focal point of the Titans' passing game.

metadata.title: Carnell Tate (stiffness) good to go for Sunday
metadata.description: Carnell Tate (stiffness) is off of the injury report and good to go for Week 1's matchup against the New York Jets.
metadata.analysis: The rookie is no longer on Tennessee's injury report and is set to make his NFL debut on Sunday. Fantasy managers should pay close attention to his debut game to see if he has the talent and situation of a breakout fantasy player for this season.

metadata.title: Carnell Tate - Spotted at practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Tate (undisclosed) was in uniform and participating in drills during Wednesday's practice, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: The rookie had been dealing with some stiffness late in the preseason but seems to be trending in the right direction as the Titans' season-opener approaches. Official word on whether Tate was a full or limited participant will come after the Titans release their practice report later Wednesday afternoon.

metadata.title: Carnell Tate Should See Heavy Usage as a Rookie
metadata.description: The fourth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Tennessee Titans rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate is expected to play a significant role in his team's passing game right away. The 21-year-old proved his big-play ability in his final collegiate season at Ohio State, recording 51 catches for 875 yards and nine touchdowns across 11 games. While the Titans have a pair of capable veteran pass-catchers in wide receivers Wan'Dale Robinson and Calvin Ridley, Tate profiles as the team's highest-upside target earner. The Titans offense as a whole should also improve in quarterback Cam Ward's second NFL season and offensive coordinator Brian Daboll's first year in Tennessee. Daboll has also shown he is willing to heavily feature a rookie wide receiver, as New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers saw 170 targets as a rookie under Daboll's watch. All in all, Tate profiles as a fantasy WR3 with significant upside entering his rookie season.
